subject: Nanotechnology
title: Physical Vapor Deposition
description: A quick, practical guide to Physical Vapor Deposition.

hook.text: Heat a metal until it evaporates, and atoms fly through vacuum to coat a surface one layer at a time.

buildup.text: Physical vapor deposition, or PVD, creates thin films by vaporizing a source material in a vacuum chamber.

discovery.text: Sputtering is a PVD variant — argon ions knock atoms off a target, depositing them on the wafer.

twist.text: PVD deposits line-of-sight — shadowed areas get no coating, making complex 3D structures difficult.

climax.text: Despite this limit, PVD deposits the metal interconnects that wire billions of transistors together.

punchline.text: Vaporize metal, catch it on silicon — that is how chips get wired.

quiz.question: What is a limitation of physical vapor deposition?
options: It can only deposit organic materials
It coats line-of-sight, missing shadowed areas on complex shapes
